identity.title: A Snapshot of Influence: A Local Data Attribution Framework for Online Reinforcement Learning

problem.claim: Online RL has sample inefficiency, training instability, and limited interpretability; the paper studies data attribution for PPO-based online RL.

gap.claim: Existing data-attribution methods assume fixed datasets, unlike online RL where experiences affect both policy updates and future data collection.

contributions.claim: A local attribution framework interprets checkpoints using records in the recent training buffer and estimates record influence through gradient similarity to action and cumulative-return targets.
The framework is applied to diagnose learning, analyze how behavior forms over time, and intervene during training.
Iterative influence-based filtering (IIF) repeatedly filters experiences to refine online RL policy updates.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors state that they initiate the study of data attribution for online RL and introduce a local attribution framework for this setting.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report that IIF reduces sample complexity, accelerates training, and produces higher returns across classic-control, navigation, locomotion, and RLHF benchmarks.

narrative_sequence.summary: Online RL is useful in complex, safety-critical domains but faces efficiency, stability, and interpretability challenges.
Fixed-dataset attribution assumptions fail because online experiences influence both learning and subsequent data collection.
The paper introduces local checkpoint attribution over the recent buffer, using action and return targets with gradient-similarity scores.
The framework supports diagnosis, temporal analysis, and intervention, and motivates the iterative filtering algorithm IIF.
The authors report broad benchmark gains in sample complexity, training speed, and return, extending to RLHF for language models.

source_observation.claim: The paper limits attribution to records in the recent training buffer and defines separate targets for action and cumulative return.

lessons.interpretation: A local scope plus behavior-specific targets can make attribution more operational and aligned with distinct diagnostic questions.
lessons.application: When studying evolving-data systems, define the attribution window explicitly and use separate target functions for immediate behavior and long-horizon outcomes.
lessons.exception: This may be unsuitable when long-range effects outside the recent buffer are central or when the target cannot be decomposed reliably.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify benchmark baselines, quantitative gains, statistical uncertainty, or the exact definition of sample complexity and training speed.
The framework's attribution accuracy, computational overhead, and behavior outside the recent training buffer are not reported.
